top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Schleck Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.

Road-specific control matters at Schleck Gran Fondo. Practice on short-steep Ardennes rollers on asphalt: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 98 miles.
80ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
7,874ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Schleck Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Schleck Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 98, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
7,874ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Schleck Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on short-steep Ardennes rollers on asphalt can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,874ft of climbing on short-steep Ardennes rollers on asphalt does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 7,874ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: May in Mondorf-les-Bains, Luxembourg — Luxembourg May delivers 50-68°F temps ideal for hard efforts, but pack arm warmers for morning chills and rain that turns Ardennes roads slick. Perfect weather fueled past epics, though cramps lurk if hydration slips. Annual variance demands flexibility. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Schleck Gran Fondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Schleck Gran Fondo’s 98 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Schleck Gran Fondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Schleck Gran Fondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on short-steep ardennes rollers on asphalt to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 98 miles of short-steep ardennes rollers on asphalt in Mondorf-les-Bains, Luxembourg.
